questions.text: What is the defining physical characteristic of a 'handheld device'?
options: It can fit in a backpack
It can be operated within the palm of one hand
questions.hint: Think about the literal meaning of 'handheld' and how the device is held during use.

questions.text: Which wearable category describes garments with built-in biometric circuitry that can also adjust fabric features based on ambient temperature?
questions.hint: Focus on the word 'garments' — this category integrates electronics directly into the fabric itself.

questions.text: Which touchscreen technology is activated by ANY input object but has the LOWEST image clarity?
questions.hint: This technology uses two layers that press together when touched — the outer layer is susceptible to scratches and reduces clarity.

questions.text: The touch interaction technique that benefits motor-impaired individuals by allowing target selection via dragging across the target is called:
questions.hint: The name suggests 'crossing' over or through the target rather than tapping it directly.

questions.text: P-Cap touchscreens are susceptible to which interference?
questions.hint: P-Cap uses a 3D electrostatic field — think about what types of electromagnetic signals could disrupt this field.

questions.text: An auditory display technique that performs a 'direct translation' of a raw data waveform to the audible domain is called:
questions.hint: The term contains 'audio' and the technique is about directly converting the waveform without additional mapping layers.

questions.text: The term 'Earcon' was coined in 1985 by D.A. Sumikawa as a pun on which visual interface element?
questions.hint: Think about the visual equivalent — what do we call a small picture that represents a concept in a GUI? The pun replaces the visual prefix with 'ear'.

questions.text: A Geiger counter using click RATE to indicate radiation levels is an example of which auditory interface type?
questions.hint: This technique maps data parameters (radiation intensity) to sound parameters (click rate) — a structured non-speech audio representation.

questions.text: Which stage of the Auditory Interface Processing Loop handles conversion of data into sound waves before reaching the speaker?
questions.hint: Look for the stage that specifically handles 'rendering' or converting data into sound — the stage just before the physical speaker output.

questions.text: QR codes were invented in 1994 by Denso Wave. What was the ORIGINAL purpose?
questions.hint: Think about what industry Denso Wave was part of (Toyota Group) — the QR code was designed for use in manufacturing and logistics.

questions.text: Which QR Code error correction level corrects up to 30% of damage — best for codes with embedded logos?
questions.hint: The highest error correction level is named after the word 'High' — it provides the most redundancy for damaged or logo-covered codes.

questions.text: In Python's itertools, which function produces all possible ORDERED arrangements of elements?
questions.hint: The word 'ordered' is key — if order doesn't matter, you'd use combinations; if order matters, use this function.

questions.text: How many total permutations exist for a set of 4 unique items?
questions.hint: Calculate 4! (4 factorial) = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1.

questions.text: Which best describes the difference between Visual Sensation and Visual Perception?
options: Sensation is subjective; Perception is consistent for all
Sensation is physical (same for all); Perception is mental/psychological (varies by person)
Sensation occurs in the brain; Perception occurs in the retina
questions.hint: Think of the camera analogy — the sensor captures the same raw data for everyone, but how each person interprets that photo can be very different.

questions.text: Which UI design principle based on the visual system states that interactive components must stand out sharply from their background?
questions.hint: The principle is about making interactive elements visually distinct — think about what 'stands out sharply' means in terms of visual design.

questions.text: In the grouper() function, what does it.zip_longest() use to pad the final chunk when the input runs short?
options: The last element of the iterable
questions.hint: The function name 'zip_longest' suggests it handles mismatched lengths — look at what parameter controls the padding value.

questions.text: The grouper() recipe works by creating n references to the SAME iterator. What is the key benefit?
options: Allows parallel processing of multiple iterators
Each reference consumes the next element, forming non-overlapping chunks
Creates independent data copies for each chunk
questions.hint: When multiple references point to the same iterator, they advance it together — this ensures each element appears in exactly one chunk, without overlap.

questions.text: Which touchscreen type provides the HIGHEST image clarity because it adds NO overlay layer on the display?
questions.hint: This technology uses beams projected across the screen surface — nothing is physically layered on top of the display itself.

questions.text: When decoding a QR code with OpenCV, which method returns the decoded data, corner points, AND the straightened QR image?
questions.hint: The method name suggests it both 'detects' and 'decodes' — it returns a tuple with data, points, and a straightened image.

questions.text: A Voicemail System's functionality extends beyond storing messages. Which statement is accurate?
options: It can only play back recorded messages
It can deliver voice info AND process transactions for individuals, orgs, products, and services
It requires a smartphone app to function
It converts speech to text automatically
questions.hint: Think about the broader definition — voicemail systems can be used for more than just leaving messages; they can act as interactive voice response systems.

questions.text: The three bold corner squares in every QR code that tell the scanner its orientation are called:
questions.hint: These patterns help the scanner 'find' the code and determine how it's rotated.

questions.text: The auditory display type that interprets a raw data sequence directly as an audio waveform is:
questions.hint: This technique directly translates data to sound without an intermediate mapping layer.

questions.text: The Wigdor & Wixon (2011) principle stating the device interface should feel like a natural extension of the user's body is called:
questions.hint: This principle is about the device feeling like a natural part of the user, not a separate tool.

questions.text: The default error correction level used by the Python qrcode library (corrects up to 15%) is:
questions.hint: The constant name in the Python library follows a pattern: ERROR_CORRECT_? where ? is a single letter representing the error level.

questions.text: The component that transforms perceived information into meaningful action — encompassing memory, reasoning, and decision-making:
questions.hint: This is the 'highest' level of the visual pipeline — it's what turns perception into action and thought.

questions.text: The itertools function used inside grouper() that pairs elements from multiple iterators and pads shorter ones:
questions.hint: This function 'zips' iterables together but handles unequal lengths by padding.

questions.text: The year the Apple iPhone and Microsoft Surface were simultaneously launched, marking the mainstream touch breakthrough:
questions.hint: This was the year that marked a major milestone in touch interfaces — both products were released around the same time.

questions.text: The outer white safety margin of a QR code (minimum 4 modules wide) that helps scanners locate the code is called the:
questions.hint: This is the empty border around the QR code that ensures the scanner can distinguish the code from its surroundings.

questions.text: Enumerate the 4 types of Auditory Interfaces covered in Module 4 (any order, comma-separated):
questions.hint: Think about the four auditory techniques discussed: one is direct data translation, one maps data to sound, one is a sound-based icon, and one uses voice.

questions.text: The Python class from OpenCV used to create a QR code detector object is:
questions.hint: The class name follows the OpenCV pattern — cv2.??? where the name describes a detector for QR codes.
